clue.text: Navigation around both poles taking up too much space

indicators.note: the navigation word is wrapped around the poles, which sit inside it

parts.note: map reading is the business of navigating with a chart
N and S, north and south, are the two poles

explanation.surface: A trip across the Arctic and Antarctic that sprawls over too much ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern coinage describes a man sitting with legs wide apart, hogging seats on public transport.

clue.text: An upturn of humour and a touch of ridicule opposing military action

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the humour word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: wit is clever humour

indicators.note: just a touch, the first letter, of ridicule is used

explanation.surface: A comedian's satirical turn mocking the generals.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upturn of' means reading upwards, giving TIW.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against war is exactly being opposed to military action, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Simple boat, one following South on some current

indicators.note: the word for one comes after the other pieces

parts.note: an amp, short for ampere, is a measure of electric current
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A basic vessel heading south on an ocean current.
explanation.definitionFit: A light flat-bottomed boat used in Chinese and Southeast Asian waters is a plain, simple craft.

clue.text: Most here may appear doddery

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters of the preceding words totter into a new order

explanation.surface: A wry remark that most residents somewhere look frail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters of 'Most here' rearranged, and a description of an old people's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a home for the elderly are often frail and unsteady, so the whole clue paints the place.

clue.text: Contender coming at rear of a run — but definitely turning up!

indicators.note: the contender word is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a rival is a contender

explanation.surface: A competitor showing up late, at the back of a race, but definitely present.
explanation.definitionFit: A coming, or appearance, is what turning up means as a noun phrase: the act of reaching a place.

clue.text: Gold carried by climber is a sought-after substance

indicators.note: the gold is held within the climbing plant word

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold carried up a mountain by a mountaineer, a precious find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusk material has long been prized, hence poached and traded illegally.

clue.text: Educator shall mostly go wrong in research institute

indicators.note: to go wrong is to go astray, so the letters stray into a new order
most of the word, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A teacher who will mostly err when doing research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SHALL to SHAL; EDUCATOR, SHAL and GO are then rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A university division for postgraduate study and research is a kind of research institution.

clue.text: Make holes in new pendant? That's sweet

parts.note: to pepper something is to riddle it with holes
mint condition means brand new
a drop is a hanging ornament such as an earring pendant

explanation.surface: Piercing a new necklace charm and calling it lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's sweet' looks like approval, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured boiled confection is a type of sweet, British for a candy.

clue.text: Way of handling professional item of kit limiting source of complaints

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: the item of kit encloses, or limits, the first letter of complaints

parts.note: a tool is an item in a kit

indicators.note: the source, or first letter, of complaints

explanation.surface: A professional's gear for dealing with grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A set procedure or code of conduct is a prescribed way of dealing with matters.

clue.text: Not speaking about arriving back showing a boob

indicators.note: the assembled letters are read backwards
the not-speaking word goes about, around, the arriving abbreviation

parts.note: mute means silent
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: A silent guest returning home, revealing a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'back' work in turn: the container makes MUTARRE, read backwards. 'Boob' is British slang for a blunder, not anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint or mistake in a printed text is a blunder, which boob means in British slang.

clue.text: Fleshy excrescence and mark on skin not caught before unconsciousness

indicators.note: the first part comes before the unconsciousness word
not marks the letter for caught as removed

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a coma is a deep unconsciousness

explanation.surface: A medical note about a lump and a skin mark found before a patient went under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not caught' drops C from SCAR to leave SAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A malignant tumour of connective tissue is a fleshy growth, the literal Greek sense.

clue.text: Past holding one in prison

indicators.note: the past abbreviation holds the one inside it

parts.note: pt is the grammatical abbreviation for past tense
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former inmate's record of time served.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit is slang for a prison or dungeon, as in a deep hole where captives are kept.

clue.text: Inquisitive shopper's request for anything else

definitions.meaning: a browsing customer asking a trader what is in stock
a catch-all for other unspecified things, like 'and so on'

explanation.surface: A customer asking what else is available.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase ends a list to cover other unnamed items, and is also a literal question to a seller.

clue.text: 60% of army unit restricted by red tape

indicators.note: the army unit fragment is held in by the colour word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: three of the five letters of the unit word are kept, from the front

parts.note: a corps is an army unit

explanation.surface: A military unit hamstrung by bureaucracy, the familiar red tape complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' leaves COR. 'tape' looks part of 'red tape' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A recording on magnetic tape is a record; to tape something is also to record it.

clue.text: Understood one politician's following the rules

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is Member of Parliament
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Accepted that a single politician is playing it by the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoken but implied, tacitly understood, is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Pass either side of church organ, describing part of same

indicators.note: the pass word sits on both sides of the church abbreviation

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Walking past a church to reach its organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'same' refers back to the organ, the ear; the adjective relates to its snail-shaped inner part.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the spiral cavity of the inner ear, part of the hearing organ just mentioned.

clue.text: Standard way to catch cold in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

indicators.note: the way word catches the cold letter inside it

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A standard route to catching a chill, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is idiom or jargon, a particular style or way of talking.

clue.text: Shetlander, say, is slim, welcoming kinky sex

indicators.note: the slim word takes in the kinky sex letters

parts.note: lean means slim
S and M, sadomasochism, is kinky sex

explanation.surface: A racy description of a thin Scottish islander enjoying unusual pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the Shetlander as one example; Shetland is an island group north of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on an island is an island dweller, and a Shetland resident is one instance.

clue.text: Rowed, delighted to be around river

indicators.note: the delighted word goes around the river letter

parts.note: stoked is slang for thrilled
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An oarsman thrilled to be out on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the pace in a rowing crew as its stroke oar is to have rowed in that seat.

clue.text: Political group curtailed movement to retain University College

indicators.note: the shortened word keeps the college letters inside it
curtailed means docked of its tail, its last letter

parts.note: a cause is a campaign or movement
UC is the abbreviation for University College

explanation.surface: A shortened campaign staying on at a London college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts CAUSE to CAUS, which then holds UC.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed meeting of party members, or the faction itself, is a political grouping.

clue.text: Tear up with story set in studio

indicators.note: the story word is set inside the jumbled letters
up here means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Ripping up a tale on the set of a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the anagram signal, giving ATER, and 'set in' is the container; 'Tear' is the rip, not a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's workshop is a studio, the French word for it.

clue.text: Angle restricting university water source

indicators.note: the angle word holds the university letter in

parts.note: a facet is an aspect or angle

explanation.surface: A viewpoint limiting a university's water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap, in American usage, is where water comes out, a source of water in the home.

clue.text: I.e. seem later at work, working over a period

indicators.note: at work means being worked on, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An excuse for seeming to arrive late at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-release drug acts gradually, its effect spread out over time rather than all at once.

clue.text: Stage performer in Wagner role (start of Ring)

parts.note: Mime is the Nibelung dwarf in Wagner's Ring cycle

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Ring is taken

explanation.surface: A performer in a Wagner opera at the start of the Ring cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts out a story without words is a mimic, a theatre performer.

clue.text: Note: 50% reduced, after setback

indicators.note: a setback reverses the letters, reading them backwards
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: A memo reporting a fifty per cent cut after a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts HALF to HAL; 'after setback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa the sixth degree of the scale is a musical note.

clue.text: Pie maker filling small kitchen pot

indicators.note: pie is the printer's term for jumbled type, so the following word is jumbled

parts.note: a filling is what is in something, giving in

explanation.surface: A baker putting the filling into a little dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie' looks like food, but in printing pie is scrambled type, so MAKER becomes RAMEK.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ovenproof dish for baking and serving individual portions is a little cooking pot.

clue.text: Smartness leading to a success in US city

indicators.note: the smartness word comes first

parts.note: chic is stylishness
go as in 'make a go of it', a success

explanation.surface: Style as the route to success in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Illinois city on Lake Michigan is an American city.

clue.text: Clear about Queen coming, perhaps

indicators.note: the clear word goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: pure means clear, unclouded
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
an advent is a coming or arrival

explanation.surface: A clear sign that the Queen may be arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning possibly or by chance, a synonym of maybe.
